the production of transuranium and superheavy elements in nuclear explosions can be significantly improved by using binary starting target compositions, including heavy components.

the development and application of mathematical models for calculating the production of heavy and super-heavy elements in the high intensity neutron fluxes of the explosive processes.

the experimental results obtained at the time are not sufficient to make a definite conclusion on the possibility of the synthesis of the superheavy nuclei.
the experimental data of the nuclear explosions, as well as of all other experiments, do not confirm the possibility of the superheavy nuclei production.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most probable production of heavy nuclei with A > 250 in nuclear explosion is possible in case of the presence of binary mixtures with the addition of heavy starting isotopes.

the production of heavy and super-heavy elements with A > 270 in nuclear explosions is only possible in the case of binary starting target mixture with the significant addition to the main isotope of curium or californium, which is not the case in Mike, Par and Babel experiments.

in order to produce superheavy elements in nuclear explosions the binary mixture of starting materials with the significant addition heavy components, such the long-lived isotopes curium or californium, should be used.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the production of the superheavy elements with atomic number A = 295 in the nuclear explosions is possible only in case of using binary mixture of starting target isotopes with significant addition of long-lived curium or californium isotopes.
it is possible to synthesize superheavy elements in the nuclear explosion with the yield ~ 10−12 g.

the production of superheavy nuclei with A ~ 300 in the Mike, Par and Barbela explosions is possible only if the starting target mixture is a mixture of binary components with significant additions of heavy isotopes of curia or californium, and the yield of these elements is very small.
